records.scope: Named Afflict keyword; tier judgment informed by Wizards' broader blocked-damage category and checked against the saved Scryfall card history.

rationale.W: No native design or explicit grant attributed to W appears in the complete scoped card review. This is no support in this sample, not a claim that W can never receive Afflict.
rationale.U: Eternal of Harsh Truths and Spellweaver Eternal give blue native Afflict at common and uncommon in Hour of Devastation. rationale.B: Ammit Eternal, Khenra Eternal, and Merciless Eternal establish black’s original Afflict branch, while Lazotep Sliver and Lost Monarch of Ifnir later grant it. The continued black evidence supports Secondary over Primary; five cards alone do not promote the tier.
rationale.R: Frontline Devastator, Manticore Eternal, Neheb, and Wildfire Eternal make Afflict an attack-and-block decision in red. Mechanical Color Pie 2021 places red Primary for the broader blocked-damage category while explicitly discussing Afflict. That direct contextual bridge supports Primary over Secondary, not a comparison of card totals.
rationale.G: No native design or explicit grant attributed to G appears in the complete scoped card review. This is no support in this sample, not a claim that G can never receive Afflict.

records.summary: Afflict makes blocking costly even when the attacker does not deal combat damage to the defending player. Red is the best-supported primary home, black has established secondary access, and blue is a set-specific tertiary case. The judgment weighs design commentary and card history; it does not turn card counts into tiers.
limitations: The 2021 article ranks the broader blocked-damage category and explicitly discusses Afflict within it. Applying that hierarchy to the named keyword is this review's inference, not a separate official Afflict ranking.

records.name: Ascend
records.scope: Saved Scryfall unique-card keyword and Oracle query population; released paper drives WUBRG decisions.

rationale.W: Skymarcher Aspirant, Snubhorn Sentry, Pride of Conquerors, and Radiant Destiny use Ascend for combat, creatures, and tribal payoff across Rivals of Ixalan. Ocelot Pride later repeats the keyword, making white Primary rather than a one-set Secondary.
rationale.U: Secrets of the Golden City, Slippery Scoundrel, Spire Winder, and Timestream Navigator cover card draw, evasion, creatures, and a mythic payoff in Rivals of Ixalan. Detective of the Month later repeats blue Ascend, supporting Primary rather than a set-bound Secondary.
rationale.B: Dusk Charger, Golden Demise, Mausoleum Harpy, Twilight Prophet, and Vona’s Hunger place Ascend on creature growth, a one-sided sweeper, death payoff, card-drain engine, and edict effect in Rivals of Ixalan. The common-through-mythic, varied-role original implementation meets the protocol’s broad-original Primary case. It is Primary rather than Secondary without relying on a later-release requirement.
rationale.R: The saved screen observes Storm Fleet Swashbuckler, Tilonalli's Summoner for red, but the evidence does not establish an independent role strong enough to distinguish Tertiary from uncertainty. The tier is left unresolved.
rationale.G: The saved screen observes Tendershoot Dryad, Wayward Swordtooth for green, but the evidence does not establish an independent role strong enough to distinguish Tertiary from uncertainty. The tier is left unresolved.

records.summary: White, blue and black each have broad original implementations and are proposed Primary. Red and green native access is retained without an unsupported Tertiary label.
limitations: Windy City Aven and Windy City Elemental are event-specific Ascend variants; they are qualified context and do not drive the primary homes. Colorless lands and equipment are separate; Ascend from Avernus is an unrelated name hit.

records.name: Assemble
records.scope: Complete Unstable special-set population; this special scope, not ordinary paper, drives every decision.

rationale.W: Aerial Toastmaster, Midlife Upgrade, and Riveting Rigger provide white assembling roles at common and uncommon in the complete Unstable-only scope. They are established support inside that special-set implementation, but lack red’s dedicated Rigger breadth, so Secondary rather than Primary.
rationale.U: Chipper Chopper, Crafty Octopus, Incite Insight, Spell Suck, and Very Cryptic Command spread blue Assemble across creature, spell, and rare roles in Unstable. This supports established special-scope access; it remains Secondary because the original implementation centers the named Rigger suite in red.
rationale.B: Finders, Keepers, Overt Operative, and Steady-Handed Mook give black three original Unstable roles from common to uncommon. That is more than an exception, but is narrower than red’s dedicated Contraption identity, supporting Secondary.
rationale.R: Steamflogger Temp, Steamflogger of the Month, Steamfloggery, Work a Double, and Wrench-Rigger make red the dedicated Rigger/Contraption implementation in Unstable across common through rare. That concentrated original role makes red Primary rather than merely one of the supporting colors.
rationale.G: First Pick, Joyride Rigger, and Steamflogger Service Rep establish green assembly roles at common and uncommon in Unstable. The complete special-scope sample supports Secondary access, not a Primary claim competing with red’s much more dedicated Rigger implementation.

records.summary: Within Unstable’s Contraption environment, red is proposed Primary and the other colors Secondary. These scoped judgments do not describe ordinary-paper keyword availability.
limitations: Special-set scope does not imply ordinary Commander legality. Cogmentor and Suspicious Nanny only reassemble. Steamflogger Boss doubles another assembly source and is retained as contextual red support, not a native source.

records.name: Assist
records.scope: Complete Battlebond multiplayer-set population plus saved later native/grant observations; the multiplayer scope drives decisions.

rationale.W: Bring Down, Dwarven Lightsmith, Play of the Game, and Skystreamer put Assist on white removal, creature, and rare spell roles in Battlebond. The deliberate common-to-rare original implementation makes white Primary within Assist’s multiplayer scope rather than a narrower Secondary.
rationale.U: Game Plan, Huddle Up, Out of Bounds, and Spellweaver Duo give blue Assist card-draw, tempo, and creature roles in Battlebond. Their deliberate rarity and role spread establishes blue as a Primary special-scope home, not merely secondary support.
rationale.B: Bloodborn Scoundrels and Fan Favorite are black common Assist creatures, while Gang Up is a black uncommon Assist sorcery. These original creature and spell roles establish Primary within Assist’s Battlebond multiplayer scope rather than Secondary.
rationale.R: Lava-Field Overlord and Magma Hellion are the original red Battlebond Assist designs, both creature applications at uncommon and common. All-Star Kicker is a Mystery Booster playtest Assist-kicker variant and is recorded separately, not used as released-paper recurrence. The two same-role original applications support Secondary rather than Primary.
rationale.G: Charging Binox gives green a creature application of Assist, while The Crowd Goes Wild applies it to a counter-granting sorcery in Battlebond. These common and uncommon designs occupy distinct roles in the original multiplayer implementation, just as black’s creature and sorcery designs do. Green is therefore proposed Primary alongside black; fewer designs alone do not justify Secondary.

records.summary: Within Battlebond’s multiplayer implementation, white, blue, black and green have varied original roles and proposed Primary homes. Red’s original applications are confined to creatures and are assessed Secondary; its later playtest variant is separate.
limitations: All-Star Kicker modifies the payment of a kicker cost and is treated as a special variant, not another ordinary Assist spell. Receiving Assist from Yume does not assign the mechanic independently to every recipient color.
Reviewed conformance record; saved timestamps are historical cutoffs, not fresh queries.

records.name: Awaken
records.scope: Saved Scryfall unique-card keyword and Oracle query population; released paper drives WUBRG decisions.

rationale.W: Sheer Drop, Encircling Fissure, Ondu Rising, and Planar Outburst give white Awaken removal, prevention, life, and mass-removal roles in Battle for Zendikar. That broad original common-to-rare implementation supports Primary rather than a narrower Secondary.
rationale.U: Rush of Ice, Clutch of Currents, Coastal Discovery, Scatter to the Winds, and Part the Waterveil give blue Awaken tempo, draw, counterspell, and mythic extra-turn roles. The original implementation spans common through mythic, making blue Primary rather than Secondary.
rationale.B: Mire’s Malice, Rising Miasma and Ruinous Path use Awaken for discard, a sweeper and targeted creature or planeswalker removal in Battle for Zendikar. That varied original implementation spans common, uncommon and rare and meets the protocol’s Primary case. Black is proposed co-Primary rather than Secondary because the evidence supplies no narrower-access restriction; a smaller card total is insufficient.
rationale.R: The saved screen observes Boiling Earth for red, but the evidence does not establish an independent role strong enough to distinguish Tertiary from uncertainty. The tier is left unresolved.
rationale.G: The saved screen observes Earthen Arms for green, but the evidence does not establish an independent role strong enough to distinguish Tertiary from uncertainty. The tier is left unresolved.

records.summary: White, blue and black each have varied original spell roles and proposed Primary homes. Red and green access is observed but remains unresolved rather than automatically Tertiary.
limitations: The 2021 land-animation entry is untouched and not mapped to Awaken. Halimar Tidecaller is support; Awaken the Inferno and Awaken the Maelstrom are unrelated name matches. Tertiary here describes narrow keyword use, not a universal rarity requirement.
